name: Kingdom of England

areaKm2.note: England and Wales ~151,000 km2 + Gascony ~20,000-30,000 + Calais Pale ~700 + the Irish Pale (mid). The world_1400 "English territory" polygon measures 287,393 km2 because it draws all of Ireland (high).

population.note: England fell from 4-5 million in 1300 by roughly half in the Black Death and later plagues (Economy of England article), giving ~2.0-2.5 million c. 1400; HYDE/OWID UK 1400 = 2.9M including Scotland. Adds Wales (~0.2M) and Gascony (~0.2-0.3M, educated guess).

urbanization.note: Urban share rose to up to 10% by 1377 (Economy of England article).

activePersonnel.note: Paid troops under arms in August 1415: Henry V's indentured expedition of at least 2,300 men-at-arms and 9,000 archers at Harfleur (Curry 2005, p. 70; infobox 11,300), plus Calais garrison (~1,000), Scottish March, Welsh castle and Gascon garrisons (~2,000-5,000, educated guess). These are contract soldiers, the standing force of the moment, not a feudal levy.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Further retinues raised by indenture and county levies under commissions of array; Henry raised ~10,000 again for 1417.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Gunners, miners, carpenters, surgeons and armourers with the expedition and crews of the ~12 royal ships.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Commissions of array could call all able men 16-60, but only a fraction were useful.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Men-at-arms: at least 2,300 with the expedition (Curry) + ~1,000 in garrisons. They rode to battle but fought dismounted at Agincourt.

quality.note: Rubric 0.75-1.0: full plate harness c. 1415, the era's best.

training.note: Rubric 0.75: veterans of Wales and Scotland in indentured retinues.

count.note: Archers: 9,000 with the expedition (Curry) + ~2,000 in garrisons. About 7,000 longbowmen stood at Agincourt (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Agincourt).

quality.note: Rubric 1.0: the English longbow massed in the field was the era's best missile weapon.

training.note: Rubric 0.75: trained archers on contract, many veterans.

count.note: Educated guess. Great guns of the Harfleur siege train (Allmand: artillery barrages forced Harfleur's surrender, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_V_of_England); exact count not found.

quality.note: Rubric 0.75: early bombards, among the best siege guns of 1415.

count.note: Educated guess. Royal ships (cogs, carracks, balingers) in 1415, before the build-up to ~30-40 by 1418-20 (Grace Dieu). The 1,500 vessels of the 1415 crossing (Allmand via Henry V article) were hired and impressed merchantmen, counted in merchantTonnage.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.75-1.0: Henry V, proven in Wales, won Agincourt against superior numbers by choice of ground and use of archers.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.75 minus: indentured retinues with strong captain loyalty; the Southampton Plot (July 1415) shows noble disaffection.

morale.note: Rubric 0.5-0.75: motivated, but dysentery at Harfleur sent ~1,330 home (Curry).

weapons.note: Anchor 4 (longbow, crossbow) plus early bombards towards anchor 5.

armor.note: Anchor 4 plus: full white plate harness, beyond the 1250 plate-and-mail anchor.

fortification.note: Anchor 4: concentric castles, Calais walls, first gunports.

logistics.note: Anchor 4: sea transport across the Channel, purveyance and supply contracts.

communications.note: Anchor 4: royal messengers and written orders.

isr.note: Anchor 4 minus: scouts and spies in France.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (via OWID): United Kingdom 1400 = 1,717, 1450 = 1,683 (2011 int$). Post-plague real wages were high; Gascony lower (low).

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Wartime: Henry V pawned crown jewels and borrowed to fund the 1415 expedition; low = peacetime crown spending share.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Woollen cloth industry, tin and lead mining.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Post-plague land abundance; pastoral shift.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the classical snapshots; medieval age structures were similar (high mortality, young population).

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Roman road network maintained by local obligation.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. London, Southampton, Bristol, Sandwich, Dover, Plymouth, Dartmouth, Hull, King's Lynn, Calais, Bordeaux.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Some 1,500 vessels assembled in the Solent for the 1415 crossing (Allmand, via the Henry V article), many foreign hires; English merchant shipping estimated at tens of thousands of tons.

supplyRangeKm.note: By analogy with Engels (isbn:0520042727, ch. 1): pre-modern armies with carts and pack animals operated ~1-2 weeks' march from a depot or navigable water.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses and oxen; the 1415 army alone took up to 20,000 horses (Agincourt article).

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2: island position, castles, walled towns and population support.

notes: Snapshot = August 1415, Henry V at Harfleur. Unlike the feudal levies of other snapshots, the 1415 army was paid indentured troops, counted as activePersonnel because they were under arms on the snapshot date. Curry (Agincourt: A New History) puts the English at ~9,000 at Agincourt vs 12,000 French; Barker, Sumption and Rogers prefer ~6,000 English (5,000 archers, 900-1,000 men-at-arms) vs 14,000-15,000 French plus up to 10,000 armed valets (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Agincourt). Population convention: England, Wales, Calais and Gascony; the Irish lordship counted only for the Pale. Same nationId as england-1066.
